evidence.text: Construct su-related dispersive sum rules, then impose st crossing using thrice-subtracted relations. Subtraction of the crossed expressions cancels EFT terms proportional to t^n with n≥3, leaving improved sum rules usable near t=−Λ².

evidence.text: Build PSD state densities by paired normal-momentum shaking and boundary projection as congruence transformations. Test a separately defined common crossing-symmetric functional on conserving partial-wave probes and nonconserving ISO(1,2) absorptive blocks.

sources.title: Gravitational positivity bounds on scalar potentials

evidence.text: Evaluate non-gravitational four-point diagrams and graviton exchange with loop-corrected 1PI scalar–scalar–graviton vertices. General-covariance Ward–Takahashi identities organize the vertex calculation; soft-momentum expansions and one- and two-loop self-energies supply the relevant coefficients.

sources.title: Causality bounds on scalar-tensor EFTs

evidence.text: Estimate coefficient sizes by normalizing dispersion relations with Λ and assigning schematic spectral-function scalings. Improved sum rules can contain mutually cancelling contributions, so the prescription surveys available rules and retains the smallest inferred scaling.

sources.title: Causality bounds on scalar-tensor EFTs

evidence.text: Expand helicity amplitudes in Wigner d-functions and use the generalized optical theorem. Integrating sum rules against optimized functions of p=√(−t) converts UV positivity into semidefinite conditions. Independent spectral channels are organized into matrices with basis {00,+0,++,+−}, separated by intermediate-state parity and even/odd spin.

sources.title: Bell inequalities in 2-2 scattering

evidence.text: Insert EFT amplitudes and numerical bootstrap amplitudes into the Bell expressions. Random MES-setting statistics are generated in Mathematica by randomizing four angular variables and maximizing over four others; the pion study also averages I3 over energy.

sources.title: Bell violation in 2 → 2 scattering in photon, gluon and graviton EFTs

evidence.text: Maps scattering amplitudes to final-state coefficients, reduces the real coefficient matrix to a Schmidt basis, and uses Appendix A's signed expression I2f=4√2(μ00μ11−μ01μ10)/Σ|μmn|². Extremization varies θ and χ subject to the initial Bell bound.

sources.title: Bell inequalities in 2-2 scattering

evidence.text: Normalize the outgoing scattering amplitudes and evaluate CGLMP joint probabilities. For the leading two-amplitude photon state, the chosen settings give I = 2√2(Φ1Φ2* + Φ2Φ1*)/(|Φ1|² + |Φ2|²), with Φ1 = g2 s² + higher orders and Φ2 = f2(s²+t²+u²) + higher orders.

sources.title: Bell violation in 2 → 2 scattering in photon, gluon and graviton EFTs

evidence.text: Uses the imported qubit CGLMP inequality, equivalent here to CHSH: local-hidden-variable models obey |I2|≤2, while the quoted quantum extremum is 2√2. Measurement phase parameters are α1=0, α2=1/2, β1=1/4 and β2=−1/4.

sources.title: Bell violation in 2 → 2 scattering in photon, gluon and graviton EFTs

evidence.text: For complex coefficients in the CP-violating analysis, switches from I2 to concurrence Δ=2|μ00μ11−μ01μ10| for a normalized pure state. Δ=0 denotes a product state and Δ=1 maximal entanglement.

evidence.text: Combine tadpole and SUSY constraints to bound winding numbers. The First Winding Number Bound constrains otherwise unbounded windings; the Two Column SUSY Bound requires at least one of two positive-column sums to be ≤T. Authors state polynomial-in-T enumeration algorithms.
